# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hoch_2014_etirinotecanPegol_ht29_mouse"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00280-014-2577-7> (open access, PMC4236622)
* Supplement: Online Resource 1 (PK/PD schematic) and Online Resource 2 (NCI-H460 PK figure), available from the article page.

Hoch 2014 compared etirinotecan pegol (NKTR-102, a PEG conjugate of irinotecan)
with conventional irinotecan in mouse xenografts. Female nude mice bearing HT29
colon or NCI-H460 lung tumors received 40 mg/kg irinotecan-equivalent IV bolus
doses of either drug on days 0, 4 and 8. Mean plasma and tumor concentrations of
etirinotecan pegol, irinotecan and SN-38 were fitted with one- to
three-compartment models in Berkeley Madonna, and a tumor PK/PD model related
the tumor SN-38 time course to tumor growth: an inhibitory Emax effect (Emax
fixed at 1) acting on Gompertz growth (Online Resource 1).

The paper contributes three models to nlmixr2lib:

| Model | Content |
|---|---|
| `Hoch_2014_etirinotecanPegol_ht29_mouse` | Tumor SN-38 PK/PD, HT29 colon xenograft |
| `Hoch_2014_etirinotecanPegol_h460_mouse` | Tumor SN-38 PK/PD, NCI-H460 lung xenograft |
| `Hoch_2014_etirinotecanPegol_tumorpk_mouse` | Descriptive two-compartment model of tumor etirinotecan pegol, HT29 (Figure 2d) |

**Read this first.** The paper prints only the PD parameters (`kgr`, `Limit`,
`EC50` per tumor line, and `Emax` = 1). It prints no PK parameter at all,
including the tumor SN-38 model that drives the PD. Every PK value in these
three models was back-solved by the maintainers from the model-predicted
curves in Figures 2 and 3. The back-solved values reproduce the paper's printed
tumor AUCs to within 4% (see [Published exposure](#published-exposure)), but
they are maintainer estimates, not the authors' estimates.

# Population

Female athymic nude mice (Ncr:Nu and Nu:Nu; 6-10 weeks, 14-28 g in the
xenograft studies) with subcutaneous HT29 or NCI-H460 tumor fragments,
randomized at a median tumor volume of 100-172 mm^3 (HT29, 13 days after
implant) or 100-245 mm^3 (NCI-H460, 9 days after implant). Each sampling time
used a group of 4 mice; blood and tumor were taken up to 60 days (HT29) or 30
days (NCI-H460) after the first dose. The models were fitted to group-mean data,
so they carry no between-animal variability and no residual-error estimate. The
total number of animals is not reported. Doses and concentrations of
etirinotecan pegol are expressed as irinotecan equivalents throughout the paper
and in these models.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Hoch_2014_etirinotecanPegol_ht29_mouse")()$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Effect `1 - Emax * C / (EC50 + C)` | n/a | Online Resource 1 schematic |
| Gompertz growth `d/dt(RTW) = kgr * RTW * log(Limit / RTW) * Effect`, `RTW(0) = 1` | n/a | Methods 'Tumor PK/PD analysis' ('based on the Gompertz equation'); equation not printed, form confirmed by reproducing the Figure 3a irinotecan-arm prediction (below) |
| `emax` (both lines) | 1 (fixed) | Methods: 'Emax was fixed at a value of 1' |
| `lkgrow` HT29 / H460 | log(0.033) / log(0.033) | Results: 'kgr ... 0.033 (day-1) ... for HT29; and 0.033 (day-1) ... for NCI-H460' |
| `ltsmax` HT29 / H460 | log(52) / log(150) | Results: 'Limit ... 52 ... for HT29; ... 150 ... for NCI-H460' |
| `lec50` HT29 / H460 | log(0.20) / log(1.2) ug/g | Results: 'EC50 ... 0.20 ug/g for HT29; ... 1.2 ug/g for NCI-H460' |
| HT29 `lka`, `lkel_sn38`, `lv_tumor_sn38` | log(0.0457), log(0.235), log(15.3) | Back-solved from Figure 3c dashed curve (maintainers) |
| HT29 `lv_tumor_sn38_irinotecan` | log(286) | 40 mg/kg / 0.140 ug/g spike height digitised from Figure 3a (maintainers) |
| HT29 `lkel_sn38_irinotecan` | log(4.2) | 3 x 0.140 ug/g / 0.100 ug day/g (Results text AUC of the irinotecan arm) |
| H460 `lka_fast`, `lka_slow`, `logitfrel`, `lkel_sn38`, `lv_tumor_sn38` | log(4.60), log(0.120), logit(0.0893), log(0.120), log(32.5) | Back-solved from Figure 3d dashed curve (maintainers) |
| H460 `lkel_sn38_irinotecan`, `lv_tumor_sn38_irinotecan` | log(0.377), log(566) | Back-solved from Figure 3b dashed curve (maintainers) |
| Tumor EP `lkel`, `lk12`, `lk21`, `lv_tumor_ep` | log(0.105), log(0.899), log(0.758), log(1.19) | Back-solved from Figure 2d solid curve (maintainers) |
| Residual errors | fixed(0) | Not reported (fits to group means) |

# Simulation

All three models are deterministic (no random effects), so a single
typical-value solve per treatment arm reproduces the paper's mean-data fits.
An etirinotecan pegol dose goes into `depot`; in the NCI-H460 model it is given
as two records of the same amount, one into `depot` and one into `depot2`,
which `f()` splits between the fast and the slow release route. Irinotecan is
dosed straight into `tumor_sn38_irinotecan`.

```{r simulate}
mod_ht29 <- readModelDb("Hoch_2014_etirinotecanPegol_ht29_mouse")
mod_h460 <- readModelDb("Hoch_2014_etirinotecanPegol_h460_mouse")
mod_tumorpk <- readModelDb("Hoch_2014_etirinotecanPegol_tumorpk_mouse")

dose_times <- c(0, 4, 8)
# Fine grid through the dosing period resolves the irinotecan SN-38 spikes
# (HT29 half-life about 4 h).
obs_grid <- function(end) sort(unique(c(seq(0, min(end, 12), by = 0.01), seq(12, end, by = 0.1))))

arm_events <- function(line, arm, end) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(obs_grid(end), cmt = "tumor_vol")
  if (arm == "Etirinotecan pegol") {
    ev <- rxode2::et(ev, amt = 40, time = dose_times, cmt = "depot")
    if (line == "NCI-H460") ev <- rxode2::et(ev, amt = 40, time = dose_times, cmt = "depot2")
  }
  if (arm == "Irinotecan") ev <- rxode2::et(ev, amt = 40, time = dose_times, cmt = "tumor_sn38_irinotecan")
  as.data.frame(ev)
}

arms <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  line = c("HT29", "NCI-H460"),
  arm = c("Vehicle", "Irinotecan", "Etirinotecan pegol")
) |>
  # One day past the last study day, so the digitised points at day 60.07
  # (HT29) and 29.93 (NCI-H460) lie inside the simulated range.
  mutate(id = row_number(), end = ifelse(line == "HT29", 61, 31))

sim_pkpd <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  a <- arms[i, ]
  mod <- if (a$line == "HT29") mod_ht29 else mod_h460
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = arm_events(a$line, a$arm, a$end), returnType = "data.frame")
  s |>
    distinct(time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    transmute(id = a$id, line = a$line, arm = a$arm, time, Ctumor_sn38, tumor_vol)
}))

ev_tep <- rxode2::et(obs_grid(60), cmt = "tumor_ep") |>
  rxode2::et(amt = 40, time = dose_times, cmt = "tumor_ep")
sim_tep <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_tumorpk, events = ev_tep, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  distinct(time, .keep_all = TRUE)

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(sim_pkpd$Ctumor_sn38), !anyNA(sim_pkpd$tumor_vol), !anyNA(sim_tep$Ctumor),
  all(sim_pkpd$tumor_vol > 0)
)
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 2d: tumor etirinotecan pegol (HT29)

```{r figure-2d}
ggplot(sim_tep, aes(time, Ctumor)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig2d_ep_tumor, aes(time, conc), shape = 1, colour = "firebrick") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Etirinotecan pegol in tumor (ug/g, irinotecan eq.)",
    title = "Tumor etirinotecan pegol after 40 mg/kg on days 0, 4, 8 (HT29)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2d of Hoch 2014. Line: packaged model; circles: digitised published prediction."
  )
```

## Figure 3: tumor SN-38 and relative tumor weight

```{r figure-3, fig.height = 6.5}
digitised_sn38 <- bind_rows(
  fig3c_ep_ht29 |> mutate(line = "HT29", arm = "Etirinotecan pegol"),
  fig3d_ep_h460 |> mutate(line = "NCI-H460", arm = "Etirinotecan pegol"),
  fig3b_irn_h460 |> mutate(line = "NCI-H460", arm = "Irinotecan")
)
sim_pkpd |>
  filter(arm != "Vehicle") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Ctumor_sn38 * 1000)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = digitised_sn38, aes(time, conc * 1000), shape = 1, colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(arm ~ line, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "SN-38 in tumor (ng/g)",
    title = "Tumor SN-38 after 40 mg/kg on days 0, 4, 8",
    caption = "Replicates the dashed curves of Figure 3a-d of Hoch 2014. Circles: digitised published prediction."
  )
```

```{r figure-3-rtw, fig.height = 4}
sim_pkpd |>
  ggplot(aes(time, tumor_vol, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig3_rtw, aes(time, rtw_fig, colour = arm), shape = 1, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~line, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Relative tumor weight", colour = NULL,
    title = "Relative tumor weight",
    caption = paste0(
      "Replicates the solid curves of Figure 3 of Hoch 2014.\n",
      "Lines: packaged model; circles: published predicted lines read off the figure."
    )
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## How closely the back-solved drivers follow the published curves

```{r driver-fit}
driver_fit <- function(sim, dig, value) {
  pred <- approx(sim$time, sim[[value]], xout = dig$time)$y
  abs(log(pred / dig$conc))
}
fits <- list(
  "Figure 3c, HT29, etirinotecan pegol" = driver_fit(
    filter(sim_pkpd, line == "HT29", arm == "Etirinotecan pegol"), fig3c_ep_ht29, "Ctumor_sn38"
  ),
  "Figure 3d, NCI-H460, etirinotecan pegol" = driver_fit(
    filter(sim_pkpd, line == "NCI-H460", arm == "Etirinotecan pegol"), fig3d_ep_h460, "Ctumor_sn38"
  ),
  "Figure 3b, NCI-H460, irinotecan" = driver_fit(
    filter(sim_pkpd, line == "NCI-H460", arm == "Irinotecan"), fig3b_irn_h460, "Ctumor_sn38"
  ),
  "Figure 2d, HT29, tumor etirinotecan pegol" = driver_fit(sim_tep, fig2d_ep_tumor, "Ctumor")
)
fit_tab <- tibble(
  curve = names(fits),
  points = vapply(fits, length, integer(1)),
  median_abs_pct = vapply(fits, function(x) 100 * median(exp(x) - 1), numeric(1)),
  max_abs_pct = vapply(fits, function(x) 100 * max(exp(x) - 1), numeric(1))
)
fit_tab |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Digitised curve" = curve, "Points" = points,
    "Median |difference| (%)" = median_abs_pct, "Max |difference| (%)" = max_abs_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

# Deterministic solves against digitised curves: the residual is digitisation
# (a pixel is 2-12 ng/g) plus the back-solve's own misfit. Medians are 0.4-3.3%;
# the largest single misses (8-24%) sit on the lowest-concentration
# points, where one pixel is a large fraction of the value. A wrong rate
# constant or volume moves the whole curve and breaks the median bound.
stopifnot(
  all(fit_tab$points > 40),
  all(fit_tab$median_abs_pct < 5),
  all(fit_tab$max_abs_pct < 30)
)
```

The Figure 3a irinotecan SN-38 spike (HT29) is narrower than one pixel and is
not digitised; it is set from its height and the paper's printed AUC (see
[Assumptions and deviations](#assumptions-and-deviations)).

# Published exposure

The Results text gives the tumor AUCs that the authors computed by
noncompartmental analysis of their predicted profiles. PKNCA on the packaged
models' profiles:

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- bind_rows(
  sim_pkpd |>
    filter(arm != "Vehicle") |>
    transmute(treatment = paste(line, arm, "SN-38"), id, time, conc = Ctumor_sn38),
  sim_tep |> transmute(treatment = "HT29 Etirinotecan pegol tumor EP", id = 99L, time, conc = Ctumor)
)
nca_dose <- nca_conc |>
  distinct(treatment, id) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = dose_times) |>
  mutate(amt = 40)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, conc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
# AUC over each study's sampling period (60 days HT29, 30 days NCI-H460), as in
# the Results text; tumor etirinotecan pegol half-life over days 20-60.
intervals <- data.frame(
  treatment = c(
    "HT29 Etirinotecan pegol SN-38", "HT29 Irinotecan SN-38", "HT29 Etirinotecan pegol tumor EP",
    "NCI-H460 Etirinotecan pegol SN-38", "NCI-H460 Irinotecan SN-38", "HT29 Etirinotecan pegol tumor EP"
  ),
  start = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 20),
  end = c(60, 60, 60, 30, 30, 60),
  auclast = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE),
  half.life = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,                          ~auclast, ~half.life,
  "HT29 Etirinotecan pegol SN-38",     31,       NA,
  "NCI-H460 Etirinotecan pegol SN-38", 26,       NA,
  "HT29 Irinotecan SN-38",             0.100,    NA,
  "NCI-H460 Irinotecan SN-38",         0.110,    NA,
  "HT29 Etirinotecan pegol tumor EP",  860,      17
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(auclast = "ug*day/g", half.life = "day"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Packaged model vs. Hoch 2014 Results text. * differs from the published value by >20%.")
```

```{r pknca-gate}
res <- as.data.frame(nca_res)
auc <- function(trt) {
  v <- res$PPORRES[res$treatment == trt & res$PPTESTCD == "auclast"]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique AUC for ", trt)
  v
}
# The three independent checks: none of these AUCs was used to back-solve.
# Measured 30.1 / 25.3 / 891 against 31 / 26 / 860. A misplaced volume, dose
# or unit moves an AUC by far more than 10%.
stopifnot(
  abs(auc("HT29 Etirinotecan pegol SN-38") / 31 - 1) < 0.10,
  abs(auc("NCI-H460 Etirinotecan pegol SN-38") / 26 - 1) < 0.10,
  abs(auc("HT29 Etirinotecan pegol tumor EP") / 860 - 1) < 0.10,
  # Not independent: the HT29 irinotecan elimination rate was set from this AUC.
  abs(auc("HT29 Irinotecan SN-38") / 0.100 - 1) < 0.02
)
```

The NCI-H460 irinotecan row is starred: the AUC implied by the paper's own
Figure 3b curve is about five times the 0.110 ug day/g printed in the text (see
[Assumptions and deviations](#assumptions-and-deviations)). The tumor
etirinotecan pegol half-life over days 20-60 is about 15 days, against the 17
days quoted in the abstract; the abstract does not say over which window its
value was estimated.

# Relative tumor weight

```{r rtw-table}
rtw_cmp <- fig3_rtw |>
  left_join(
    sim_pkpd |> mutate(time = round(time, 2)) |> select(line, arm, time, tumor_vol),
    by = c("line", "arm", "time")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (tumor_vol / rtw_fig - 1))
stopifnot(!anyNA(rtw_cmp$tumor_vol))
rtw_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Tumor" = line, "Arm" = arm, "Day" = time, "Figure 3 line" = rtw_fig,
    "Packaged model" = tumor_vol, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

irn <- filter(rtw_cmp, arm == "Irinotecan")
# Irinotecan arms: the drug effect is small, so these rows test the Gompertz
# form and the printed kgr / Limit. HT29 agrees within 4%; NCI-H460 runs 4-8%
# high.
stopifnot(max(abs(irn$pct_diff[irn$line == "HT29"])) < 6, max(abs(irn$pct_diff)) < 12)
```

The irinotecan arms confirm the growth equation: with the printed `kgr` and
`Limit`, the Gompertz form reproduces the Figure 3a prediction to within 4% at
every day read. The etirinotecan pegol arms do not match as closely. With the
printed `EC50` and the SN-38 curve the figure itself draws, the model predicts
less early growth suppression than the figure's solid line (HT29: 2.35 against
1.78 at day 28), and no single `EC50` reproduces both the flat early course and
the late regrowth of the published line. The vehicle lines are discussed under
[Assumptions and deviations](#assumptions-and-deviations).

The Results text quotes the tumor-volume increases. The packaged model:

```{r text-claims}
at_day <- function(ln, ar, d) {
  s <- filter(sim_pkpd, line == ln, arm == ar)
  approx(s$time, s$tumor_vol, xout = d)$y
}
claims <- tibble::tribble(
  ~claim,                                                     ~published, ~model,
  "HT29, etirinotecan pegol, day 60: 'only sixfold'",          6,          at_day("HT29", "Etirinotecan pegol", 60),
  "HT29, irinotecan, day 60: 'a 30-fold increase'",            30,         at_day("HT29", "Irinotecan", 60),
  "NCI-H460, etirinotecan pegol, day 30: 'only eightfold'",    8,          at_day("NCI-H460", "Etirinotecan pegol", 30),
  "NCI-H460, irinotecan, day 30: 'a >= 21-fold increase'",     21,         at_day("NCI-H460", "Irinotecan", 30)
)
claims |>
  dplyr::rename("Results text" = claim, "Published fold" = published, "Packaged model" = model) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
# Deterministic. Model 6.8 / 29.9 / 9.5 / 22.7 against 6 / 30 / 8 / >= 21;
# the text rounds to whole folds, and the etirinotecan pegol arms carry the
# early-suppression gap described above.
stopifnot(
  abs(claims$model[1] / 6 - 1) < 0.25,
  abs(claims$model[2] / 30 - 1) < 0.10,
  abs(claims$model[3] / 8 - 1) < 0.25,
  claims$model[4] >= 21
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

**No PK parameter is printed.** Every PK value in the three models was
back-solved by the maintainers from the article's figures. The values are
maintainer estimates, made by least squares on the log scale against the
digitised model-predicted curves:

- *Tumor SN-38 after etirinotecan pegol, HT29 (Figure 3c).* The paper calls this
  a two-compartment model without stating the input. A dose depot releasing
  first-order into a tumor SN-38 compartment reproduces the curve (median 1.9%
  difference). The slower rate constant, 0.0457/day, is assigned to the
  release, so the 15-day terminal decline reflects the slow loss of
  etirinotecan pegol from tumor that the paper reports (17-day half-life).
- *Tumor SN-38 after etirinotecan pegol, NCI-H460 (Figure 3d).* The curve jumps
  within hours of each dose and then keeps rising for days, which one
  first-order release cannot follow (log-scale RMSE 3.7%, with the post-dose
  jumps missed, against 1.7% for the packaged form). Two parallel release
  routes do: 8.9% of the dose at 4.6/day and the
  rest at 0.12/day. The slow release rate and the SN-38 elimination rate cannot
  be told apart from the curve (the least-squares fit runs to equality), so both
  are set to 0.120/day. The H460 and HT29 drivers therefore have different
  structures; each was chosen as the simplest form that follows its own curve.
- *Tumor SN-38 after irinotecan.* One compartment with bolus-type input, as the
  paper states. For NCI-H460 the Figure 3b curve gives 70.7 ng/g per dose and an
  elimination rate of 0.377/day. For HT29 the Figure 3a spike reaches 140 ng/g
  but falls to baseline within one pixel (about 0.3 day), so its decay cannot be
  read from the figure. The elimination rate, 4.2/day, is instead set from the
  printed AUC of that arm: 3 doses x 0.140 ug/g / 0.100 ug day/g. It is
  consistent with the text ('undetectable within 12 h'; the tumor lower limit
  of quantitation is 0.030 ug/g).
- *Tumor etirinotecan pegol, HT29 (Figure 2d).* The paper's two-compartment fit
  to tumor concentrations has a fast spike at each dose and a slow phase. The
  biexponential 19.3 exp(-1.716 t) + 14.34 exp(-0.0465 t) ug/g per 40 mg/kg
  reproduces it (median 1.7% difference). It is written as an IV bolus into the
  sampled tumor pool `tumor_ep`, which exchanges with `peripheral1`. Neither
  compartment is plasma: the authors fitted tumor data directly. The
  observation is `Ctumor`, not `Cc`, because it is a tumor concentration.
- *Apparent volumes.* `v_tumor_sn38`, `v_tumor_sn38_irinotecan` and
  `v_tumor_ep` are dose-to-concentration ratios ((mg/kg) per (ug/g)). They
  absorb the unknown fraction of each dose that reaches the tumor as the
  analyte, and are not physical volumes.
- *Not packaged.* The plasma fits (three-compartment etirinotecan pegol,
  one-compartment irinotecan; Figure 2a-c and Online Resource 2) and the tumor
  irinotecan fit (Figure 2b) are not packaged. Their terminal phases sit on
  linear axes at the floor of the plot (0-800 ug/mL for plasma etirinotecan
  pegol) and the irinotecan curves are spikes narrower than a pixel, so they
  cannot be back-solved. They are not linked to the PD model.
- *Rat and dog.* The rat and dog PK in Figure 5 was analysed only by NCA, so no
  model exists to package.

**Inconsistencies in the paper.**

- *NCI-H460 irinotecan SN-38 AUC.* The Results text gives 0.110 ug day/g, but
  the Figure 3b predicted curve (and the observed means plotted with it)
  decline with a half-life of about 1.8 days, which gives about 0.56 ug day/g
  over three doses. The packaged model follows the figure. The effect on tumor
  growth is negligible either way: SN-38 never exceeds 0.085 ug/g against an
  `EC50` of 1.2 ug/g.
- *Vehicle predictions in Figure 3.* With an inhibitory effect and one shared
  parameter set, the vehicle (no drug) prediction is the upper bound for every
  treated arm. The grey vehicle lines in Figure 3 do not follow the printed
  `kgr` and `Limit`. At HT29 day 56 the line reads about 19.6, against 27.9 from
  the printed values. At NCI-H460 day 28 it reads about 27.5, against 20.5. In
  Figure 3a the irinotecan prediction lies above the vehicle prediction, which no
  shared parameter set with an inhibitory effect can produce. The black
  irinotecan lines, by contrast, match the printed parameters (table above). So
  either the vehicle lines were drawn from a separate fit, or the legend swaps
  the line styles. The packaged models use the printed values; their vehicle
  prediction is the irinotecan curve without drug effect.
- *Etirinotecan pegol tumor-weight predictions.* See
  [Relative tumor weight](#relative-tumor-weight). The packaged models reproduce
  the text's fold increases (6.8 and 9.5 against 'sixfold' and 'eightfold') but
  run up to about 40% above the Figure 3c/3d solid lines in mid-course.

**Other assumptions.**

- The Gompertz equation is not printed (the citation given, Simeoni 2004, is not
  a Gompertz model). The form `kgr * RTW * log(Limit / RTW)` with the effect as
  a multiplier is the one that reproduces the Figure 3a irinotecan prediction
  with the printed `kgr` and `Limit` to within 4%.
- `RTW(0) = 1`: the paper fitted relative tumor volume, normalised to the volume
  at the first dose.
- No residual error or between-animal variability is reported (fits to group
  means); residual-error SDs are `fixed(0)`.
- No erratum or correction notice was found for this article (checked
  2026-11-25).
